enumeration_method: sitemap index (11 child sitemaps) union + llms.txt-only section roots; llms-full.txt page count cross-check
note: Population: the site's own sitemap index lists 11 child sitemaps whose union is 933 URLs. llms-full.txt declares the same total for itself ('the full documentation (pages 1-100 of 933)'), so two independent enumerations agree. llms.txt carries 807 of those (the versioned mirrors are not in it) plus 9 section-root URLs that appear in no sitemap, so the frontier is 933 + 9 = 942. Every page is fetched as its own .md twin (GitBook serves one per page), as are its figures, from the native asset URLs. Figure captions and alt text are the primary evidence for what a figure is; the figures that decide a verdict are opened at full size and captured. The source is a BPMN 2.0 vendor's own manual, so the recurring question is whether a figure is a capture of the Process Editor canvas (a BPMN 2.0 diagram, per the docs: 'Process Editor uses BPMN 2.0 and C# to create integration flows') or of application chrome. Currency: the unversioned pages are the 6.3.0 documentation (the site's own 'Frends 6.3' release notes and the 6.1.0/6.2.0 archives published beside them); every /docs/frends-6.x.y/ URL is an archive copy of a current page and is excluded as E3-duplicate of it. Duplicate detection is by image content, not by URL: the versioned docs live in a different GitBook space, so the same diagram re-published under 6.1.0/6.2.0 has a different asset URL and a byte-identical file, and md5 identity (or a same-path URL claim, where the archive copy's figures were not re-served) decides E3; only 3 archive pages had to fall back on the URL claim. BPMN evidence inside the corpus: 123 of the source's task-library diagrams are bpmn-js exports - the file itself begins '<!-- created with bpmn-js / http://bpmn.io -->' and carries data-element-id attributes - so those pages' notation is settled by the asset, not by a caption; their text labels were read one by one, and exactly one of the 123 carries an AI label (row n=804, OpenAI). Judgement exclusions run high (15.7%) for a structural reason: this is the manual of a BPMN 2.0 tool, so 141 pages show a genuine Process Editor diagram that contains no AI element (E2) and 7 show a non-BPMN artefact (E1). Those rows were re-examined for false negatives rather than waved through: every judged-excluded page carrying AI vocabulary was listed (24 pages), its AI sentence read, and the figure of each one looked at; two near-misses were promoted to INCLUDE (n=203, n=239, whose AI shapes sit under captions that never say 'AI'), and the rest were dismissed with the mention quoted and its real referent named in the row (the AI Code Assistant, the AI Documentation Assistant, 'AI & ML' as a connector-category heading, or the English words 'prompted'/'prompt' and the substrings inside 'WAITING' and 'embedding'). One row's reason was corrected from E2 to E0 (n=40: no figure on it is a process diagram). Known gap: the page at https://docs.frends.com/bap/general/single-sign-on publishes its only figure as src="broken://files/oH85GMcOLRjv7m4KGNcN" - a GitBook placeholder for an asset that no longer resolves - so it was judged on its caption (E0, application chrome) and cannot be visually checked until the vendor republishes it; it is in OPERATOR-TODO.md.
